title: Year 10 Business mock: Paper 1 and Paper 2 style sections (52 marks)
subject: Business
source: Written for business/y10 lessons 55, 56, 57 (Year 10 Business mock: Paper 1 and Paper 2 style sections with mark scheme (written for TGA, in the lesson and as a pupil PDF))
intro: Lessons 55 and 56. Own 4BS1-style questions written for TGA on two fictional cases. 30 minutes for each section.

bullets: Noor Bakes: a family bakery in Leicester, 12 employees, two shops
Sales of celebration cakes are growing
Staff turnover rose last year; the owner plans changes to pay and structure

questions.a: the number of subordinates directly controlled by a manager (1).

questions.q: 1b. Identify two non-financial methods of motivation.
questions.a: any two: job rotation, job enrichment, autonomy, recognition, training (2).

questions.q: 1c. Three bakers each earn £11.50 an hour for 30 hours a week. Calculate their total weekly wage cost.
1d. Explain one advantage to Noor Bakes of a flat structure.
1e. Analyse the impact on Noor Bakes of introducing commission for shop staff.
questions.a: two linked chains, e.g. higher sales motivation vs competition harming teamwork (6).

questions.q: 1f. Option 1: a bonus scheme. Option 2: job enrichment. Justify which option Noor Bakes should choose to reduce staff turnover.
questions.a: both options analysed, justified decision with 'depends on' (9).

questions.q: 1g. Explain one reason Noor Bakes uses induction training.

bullets: GreenCart plc: a UK supermarket chain (fictional) with 2,400 employees
It is considering decentralising decisions to store managers
New checkout staff are trained in their first week

questions.a: passing authority to a subordinate to carry out a task (1).

questions.q: 2b. State two features of a hierarchical structure.
questions.a: any two: many levels, narrow spans, long chain of command (2).

questions.q: 2c. Calculate GreenCart's labour turnover last year (300 left; 2,400 employees).
2d. Explain one reason GreenCart might decentralise decision making.
2e. Analyse how Herzberg's theory could help GreenCart reduce labour turnover.
questions.a: two chains on motivators such as recognition and responsibility vs hygiene factors (6).

questions.q: 2f. Evaluate whether GreenCart should train new checkout staff on the job or off the job.
questions.a: both methods weighed (cost, consistency, speed, disruption), justified judgement (9).

questions.q: 2g. Explain one role of the HR function at GreenCart.

blocks.note: Own questions in the 4BS1 style; check level descriptors against Pearson's published mark schemes.
